title: A bounded-above finite-free model of a module complex glues from a finite standard-open cover
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules. Let $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generate the unit ideal, and write $M^\bullet_{f_i}=M^\bullet\otimes_A A_{f_i}$. View complexes as objects of the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Call an object $C$ of $D(A)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(A)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^j(E^\bullet)\to H^j(C)$ for $j>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Call $C$ pseudo-coherent if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules. If every $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $M^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. If every $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is pseudo-coherent, then $M^\bullet$ is pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Fix $m$. Each local bounded finite-free witness gives cohomology vanishing above the maximum of $m$ and its upper term bound; transfer vanishing across the witness cohomology isomorphisms. Choose a common upper bound using finiteness of the index set. Apply [lem-pc-homology-vanishing-localization-span] in each degree above that bound to obtain global vanishing. This includes the empty cover.
Induct on $k\in\mathbf N$ in the assertion that any locally $m$-pseudo-coherent complex vanishing in all degrees $j\ge m+k$ is globally $m$-pseudo-coherent. For $k=0$, use the vanishing base theorem.

At $k+1$, set $n=m+k$. Apply [lem-pc-m-pseudo-coherent-localization-cone-step], giving a distinguished triangle with an $m$-pseudo-coherent source and a locally $m$-pseudo-coherent cone vanishing above $n-1$. The induction hypothesis applies to the cone. The second clause of the triangle theorem then gives $m$-pseudo-coherence of the original complex. For a global bound $b$, choose $k=\max(b-m+1,0)$; integer arithmetic verifies the needed bound.
For the pseudo-coherent clause, use the equivalence with all fixed-degree conditions locally, apply the fixed-degree descent just proved for each integer, and use the same equivalence globally.
